definitions.explanation: Mimetic word describing the involuntary shaking of the body due to cold, fear, or anger. Represents a rapid, fine vibration of the whole body or parts of it.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}くてぶるぶる{震|ふる}えた。
examples.english: I was shivering from the cold.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{怖|こわ}がってぶるぶる{震|ふる}えている。
examples.english: The dog is trembling with fear.

examples.japanese: {怒|いか}りでぶるぶると{手|て}が{震|ふる}えた。
{薄着|うすぎ}で{外|そと}に{出|で}たら、ぶるぶる{震|ふる}えが{止|と}まらなかった。
examples.english: When I went outside in light clothing, I couldn't stop shivering.

notes:
One of the most common body-related onomatopoeia in Japanese. The voiced consonant ぶ gives it a heavier, more visceral feeling than the lighter がたがた. Always involuntary — the shaking is caused by an external stimulus (cold, fear, anger) that the person cannot control.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ぶるぶる{震|ふる}える: to tremble/shiver
- ぶるぶると{震|ふる}える: to tremble (with と particle)
- {寒|さむ}さでぶるぶる: shivering from cold
- {恐怖|きょうふ}でぶるぶる: trembling with fear

SIMILAR WORDS:
- がたがた{震|ふる}える: to shiver violently — stronger, implies teeth chattering or louder shaking
- わなわな{震|ふる}える: to tremble (with emotion) — emphasizes emotional intensity, especially anger or shock
- ぷるぷる: to quiver — lighter, cuter vibration; used for jelly-like textures or small movements
